findings.rule: Title block heat treatment field must not contradict or omit referenced heat treatment notes.
findings.reasoning: The title block heat_treatment field is '---' (indicating none), yet note N1 specifies case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–2 mm case depth. This contradiction will cause the part to be manufactured without the required heat treatment.
findings.correction: Update the title block heat_treatment field to reference N1 (e.g., 'CASE HARDEN PER NOTE N1') or state the requirement directly.

findings.rule: Functional bores and bearing seats on a sleeve must have a specified tolerance or fit class.
findings.reasoning: Dimensions D3 (⌀12 inner bore) and D4/D12 (⌀20 bore) are functional diameters for a pin sleeve but carry no tolerances. Under the general machining tolerances, the ⌀12 bore would default to ±0.5 mm and the ⌀20 bore to ±0.5 mm, which is far too loose for any functional sliding or press fit.
findings.correction: Add appropriate fit-class tolerances (e.g., H7) or explicit dimensional tolerances to all functional bore diameters.

findings.rule: Thread relief/undercut is required when threads run into a shoulder or blind bottom.
findings.reasoning: Feature F4 describes an M5 threaded hole 6 mm deep. Note N1 requires threads to be kept soft during case hardening and then retapped. Tapping a blind hole after case hardening demands a thread-relief undercut at the bottom so the tap can produce full-depth threads without breaking against the hardened shoulder; none is dimensioned or called out.
findings.correction: Add a thread-relief undercut or drill-point clearance dimension at the bottom of the M5 × 6 deep hole in F4.

findings.rule: Drawing notes must contain valid engineering information.
findings.reasoning: Note N5 contains the text 'YFYFGHYFGHGF', which is gibberish. While it does not directly alter geometry, placeholder or accidental text on a released drawing creates confusion and risks misinterpretation on the shop floor.
findings.correction: Delete note N5 or replace it with the intended engineering instruction.
